3. According to prosecution version, the deceased Prem Bala (sister of informant Dheeraj Yadav)
was working as Revenue Inspector and she was posted at Tehsil Mariahu.
She was married with applicant no.1 Akhilesh Yadav on 21.05.2021.

In her marriage, a Hyundai car, jewellery worth Rs.10 lakhs and other presents like clothes etc. were given to the applicant no.1 and his family members but the applicants/accused started harassing her on account of dowry.
In month of June, 2021, the accused persons got purchased jewellery of Rs. 30,000/- from Prem Bala.
On 27.07.2021, applicant no.1 has forcibly got purchased a Royal Enfield motorcycle worth Rs.2,48,000/- from Prem Bala and for that purpose the father of informant has to break his fixed deposit.
Applicant no.1 took Rs.40,000/- from Prem Bala on pretext of treatment of his father and another amount of Rs.35,000/- was also taken for treatment of his niece.
Applicant no.1 has forcibly got purchased jewellery of Rs. two lakhs from Prem Bala.
Due to these acts, Prem Bala suffered depression.
The accused persons have even closed her entry in the matrimonial home, due to which she started residing at a rented room at Mariahu.
Later on, condition of Prem Bala started deteriorating.
In month of January, 2022, accused persons refused for her treatment.
The informant and his brother-in-law admitted Prem Bala in hospital but her condition did not improve and on 20.03.2022 she passed away while she was under treatment at hospital.
4. The first information report was registered on 04.05.2022 under Sections 498A, 306 IPC and Section  D.P. Act.

After investigation, police have prepared final report in favour of accused persons, however the Circle Officer (Police) has directed for further investigation but again the final report was prepared.
The Circle Officer has again directed for further investigation and in the similar way again final report was submitted.

It appears that again further investigation was directed in the matter and thereafter charge-sheet dated 20.03.2023 was submitted against the applicants/accused persons for offence under section 498-A IPC and section  D.P. Act.
It appears after further investigation, a supplementary charge-sheet for offence under section 306 IPC was also filed against applicants / accused persons.
5. Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that the allegations made by the informant are wholly false and no prima-facie case is made out against the applicants.
It was a love marriage between the applicant no.1 and the deceased Prem Bala and thus, there was no question of demand of any dowry.

It was submitted that deceased was suffering from breathing and chest congestion illness, due to which on 12.03.2022 applicant no.1 has admitted her in Om Sai Nath Hospital and Research Centre, Mariahu, Jaunpur.

10. Perusal of record shows that initially after investigation, police have prepared final report in favour of accused persons for two times and after further investigation charge-sheet for offence under section 498-A IPC and section  D.P. Act was submitted.
However, matter was again investigated and a supplementary charge sheet was submitted for offence under section 306 IPC.

In case of Vinay Tyagi (supra), it was held that where initial report under section 173(2) Cr.P.C is submitted before the competent court and later on the subsequent report under Section 173(8) CrPC is filed, in such matters the supplementary report, would have to be dealt with "as part of the primary report" in sub-section (3) to (6) of section 173 Cr.P.C and both the reports have to be read conjointly and it is the cumulative effect of the reports and the documents annexed thereto to which the Court would be expected to apply its mind to determine whether there exist grounds to presume that the accused has committed the offence.

In case of Luckose Zachariah (supra), referring to the case of Vinay Tyagi, the Apex Court held as under:
'' In view of the clear position of law which has been enunciated in the judgments of this Court, both in Vinay Tyagi (supra) and Vinubhai Haribhai Malaviya (supra), it is necessary for the Magistrate, to have due regard to both the reports, the initial report which was submitted under Section 173(2) as well as the supplementary report which was submitted after further investigation in terms of Section 173(8).

It is thereafter that the Magistrate would have to take a considered view in accordance with law as to whether there is ground for presuming that the persons named as accused have committed an offence.

While the High Court has relied upon the decision in Vinay Tyagi (supra), it becomes necessary for this Court to set the matter beyond any controversy having due regard to the fact that the Sessions Judge in the present case had while remitting the proceedings back to the Magistrate relied on the judgment of the Single Judge of the Kerala High Court in Joseph (supra) which is contrary to the position set out in Vinay Tyagi.

Hence, the JFCM - I Alappuzha shall reexamine both the reports in terms of the decisions of this Court in Vinay Tyagi vs Irshad Ali alias Deepak and Vinubhai Haribhai Malaviya vs State of Gujarat as noted above and in terms of the observations contained in the present judgment.

sentences.text:
At this stage it would be apt to quote provisions of section 306 IPC, which read as under:
"306. Abetment of suicide If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine."

13. From a bare reading of the provision, it is apparent that to constitute an offence under Section 306 IPC, the prosecution has to establish: (i) that a person committed suicide, and (ii) that such suicide was abetted by the accused.

The parameters of "abetment" have been provided in Section 107 of the IPC, which reads as under:
"107. Abetment of a thing A person abets the doing of a thing, who - First- Instigates any person to do that thing; or Secondly- Engages with one or more other person or persons in any conspiracy for the doing of that thing, if an act or illegal omission takes place in pursuance of that conspiracy, and in order to the doing of that thing; or Thirdly- Intentionally aids, by any act or illegal omission, the doing of that thing.
Explanation 1-

A person who by wilful misrepresentation, or by wilful concealment of a material fact which he is bound to disclose, voluntarily causes or procures, or attempts to cause or procure, a thing to be done, is said to instigate the doing of that thing."
14.

Thus, as per section 107 IPC, a person can be said to have abetted in doing a thing, if he, firstly,
instigates any person to do that thing; or secondly, engages with one or more other person or persons in any conspiracy for the doing of that thing, if an act or illegal omission takes place in pursuance of that conspiracy, and in order to the doing of that thing; or thirdly, intentionally aids,
by any act or illegal omission, the doing of that thing.
Explanation to Section 107 states that any wilful misrepresentation or wilful concealment of material fact which he is bound to disclose, may also come within the contours of "abetment".

It is manifest that under all the three situations, direct involvement of the person or persons concerned in the commission of offence of suicide is essential to bring home the offence under Section 306 of the IPC.
15.

In the instant matter, as per prosecution after condition of deceased started deteriorating on 21.01.2022 she was admitted in the hospital at Allahabad and from 12.03.2024 to 13.03.2022 she remained admitted at Om Sai Nath Hospital, Jaunpur.
From Reports of these hospitals, it appears that she was suffering from chest congestion and breathing related illness.
On 20.03.2022 she was admitted in Infinity Care hospital, Varanasi but she could not survive and passed away on the same day in hospital.
It appears that post-mortem of deceased has not been conducted.

In death certificate of deceased as well as in statement of concerned doctor, cause of death of deceased took Akhilesh Yadav And 13 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109233996/

(i) Sudden Cardio Pulmonary Arrest,
(ii) Intorsti Tial Fibcosis,
(iii) Bronchiectasis,
(iv) Type Two Respiratory Failure,
(v) Lower Respiratory Tract Infection and (v) Sepsis.

sentences.text: 16. Thus, it is apparent that the deceased has died due to the above referred six medical reasons and there is absolutely no medical evidence that deceased has committed suicide.
In fact there is no prosecution version that deceased has committed suicide.

Merely because the informant and his family members have alleged that due to harassment of deceased by the accused persons, the deceased was driven to depression and illness and she died of illness, would not satisfy the ingredients of offence under section 306 IPC.
Thus, when it is clear that the deceased has not committed suicide, the question of applicability of section 306 IPC does not arise.
If deceased did not commit suicide rather she died of illness, the accused persons can not prosecuted for offence under section 306 IPC.
Therefore, no prima facie case under section 306 IPC is made out against the applicants/ accused.

It was alleged due to these acts, Prem Bala suffered depression and that the accused persons have even closed her entry in the matrimonial home, due to which she had started residing at a rented room at Mariahu.
Despite all these facts applicants continued harassment of the deceased and later on, condition of Prem Bala deteriorated.
In month of January, 2022, accused persons refused for her treatment.

The informant and his brother-in-law admitted Prem Bala in hospital at Allahabad but her condition did not improve and 20.03.2022 she was shifted to Infinity Care hospital, Varanasi but her condition did not improve and she passed away while she was under treatment at hospital.

sentences.text: The legal position on the issue of quashing of criminal proceedings is well-settled that the jurisdiction to quash a complaint, first information report or a charge-sheet should be exercised sparingly and only in exceptional cases.

However, where the allegations made in the FIR or the complaint and material on record even if taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused, the charge-sheet may be quashed in exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.

In well celebrated judgement of State of Haryana and others Vs. Ch. Bhajan Lal AIR 1992 SC 605, Hon'ble Apex Court has carved out certain guidelines, wherein FIR or proceedings may be quashed but cautioned that the power to quash FIR or proceedings should be exercised sparingly and that too in the rarest of rare cases.

It has been held that if a prima facie case is made out disclosing ingredients of the offence, court should not quash the charge sheet/complaint.

In case of Venkateshwaran (supra), the Apex has observed that disputed questions of fact could not be examined under section 482 CrPC.
19.

In case of Geeta Mehrotra & Anr. Vs. State of UP & Anr.(supra), it was observed:-
"20.

Prasad & Ors. reported in (2000) 3 SCC 693 wherein also in a matrimonial dispute, this Court had held that the High Court should have quashed the complaint arising out of a matrimonial dispute wherein all family members had been roped into the matrimonial litigation which was quashed and set aside.

Their Lordships observed therein with which we entirely agree that:
"there has been an outburst of matrimonial dispute in recent times.
Marriage is a sacred ceremony, main purpose of which is to enable the young couple to settle down in life and live peacefully.

But little matrimonial skirmishes suddenly erupt which often assume serious proportions resulting in heinous crimes in which elders of the family are also involved with the result that those who could have counselled and brought about rapprochement are rendered helpless on their being arrayed as accused in the criminal case.

There are many reasons which need not be mentioned here for not encouraging matrimonial litigation so that the parties may ponder over their defaults and terminate the disputes amicably by mutual agreement instead of fighting it out in a court of law where it takes years and years to conclude and in that process the parties lose their "young" days in chasing their cases in different courts."

The view taken by the judges in this matter was that the courts would not encourage such disputes."
20.

In case of Kahkashan Kausar (supra) after considering several earlier judgments, the Apex Court held:
Akhilesh Yadav And 13 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 9 September, 2024

. The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes,
without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.
Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them.
19. Coming to the facts of this case, upon a perusal of the contents of the FIR dated 01.04.19, it is revealed that general allegations are levelled against the Appellants.
The complainant alleged that 'all accused harassed her mentally and threatened her of terminating her pregnancy'.

Furthermore, no specific and distinct allegations have been made against either of the Appellants herein, i.e., none of the Appellants have been attributed any specific role in furtherance of the general allegations made against them.
This simply leads to a situation wherein one fails to ascertain the role played by each accused in furtherance of the offence.
The allegations are therefore general and omnibus and can at best be said to have been made out on account of small skirmishes.
Insofar as husband is concerned, since he has not appealed against the order of the High court, we have not examined the veracity of allegations made against him.
However, as far as the Appellants are concerned, the allegations made against them being general and omnibus, do not warrant prosecution.

21. Keeping in view aforesaid legal position, in the instant matter it appears from first information report that mainly the allegations of dowry demand and harassment of deceased have been levelled against applicant No. 1, who is husband of deceased.
Entire family of applicant No.1 and even the relations have been named in the first information.

From the facts it appears that the alleged jewellery of Rs. 30,000/- was also got purchased from Prem Bala at the instance of applicant No. 1 /
husband and similarly the alleged Royal Enfield motorcycle was also got purchased from deceased Prem Bala by the applicant No. 1 / husband.

The allegation of taking money from the deceased on pretext of providing treatment to his family members is also attributed to the applicant No. 1 /
husband.
There is no cogent specific allegation against applicant No. 2 to 14.
These applicants include father-in-law, mother-in-law, brother-in-law and sister-in-law of informant.
It is not disputed that since before the incident, the deceased was residing separately.
Even otherwise, the sisters-in-law (nanad) and brothers-in-law of deceased were not going to be benefited by fulfilment of any demand.

Considering entire facts of the matter and above refereed case of Geeta Mehrotra (supra) and Kahkashan Kausar (supra), no prima facie case is made out against applicant No. 2 to 14, who are family members / relatives of the husband of deceased.

23. So far the applicant No. 1 is concerned, he is husband of the deceased and there are several allegations against him and on various occasions, as alleged in the first information report, he has forced the deceased to purchase jewellery / motorcycle and to part with her money.
Substantially all the allegations have been levelled against him.

Considering entire material on record a case under Akhilesh Yadav And 13 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109233996/
8 section 498-A IPC and section  D.P. Act is made out against applicant No. 1.

sentences.text: At this stage it could also not be said that impugned criminal proceeding under section 498-A IPC and section  D.P. Act are manifestly attended with mala fide and instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the applicant No.1 with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge.

It is well settled that the High Court cannot embark upon the appreciation of evidence while considering the petition filed under Section 482 CrPC for quashing criminal proceedings and if a prima facie case is made out disclosing the ingredients of the offence alleged against the accused
, the Court cannot quash a criminal proceeding.

The submissions raised by learned counsel for the applicants on behalf of applicant No. 1 call for determination on questions of fact which may be adequately discerned either through proper investigation or which may be adjudicated upon only by the trial court and even the submissions made on points of law can also be more appropriately gone into only by the trial court.

24. In view of aforesaid the impugned proceedings, including charge-sheet and cognizance /
summoning order, against applicant No. 2 to 14 are hereby quashed.
25. The cognizance / summoning order so far it relates to offence under section 306 IPC against applicant No. 1 Akhilesh Yadav, is also quashed.
26. The case for offence under section 498 -A IPC and section 3/ 4 D.P. Act against applicant No. 1 Akhilesh Yadav shall proceed further in accordance with law.
27. The application under section 482 CrPC is disposed of in above terms.
